findings.title: Oracle Security Alert Advisory - CVE-2026-35273
findings.summary_md: Oracle's out-of-band Security Alert, initially released June 10, 2026, fixes CVE-2026-35273 in PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools 8.61 and 8.62. The flaw is remotely exploitable without authentication over HTTP and leads to remote code execution, rated CVSS 9.8, in the Updates Environment Management component. Credit for the report goes to researchers at Trend Zero Day Initiative and Trend Research.

findings.title: ShinyHunters Exploits Oracle PeopleSoft Zero-Day (CVE-2026-35273) to Trigger Extortion
findings.summary_md: Reported that ShinyHunters exploited the Oracle PeopleSoft zero-day CVE-2026-35273 before Oracle's June 10 advisory, using it for data theft and extortion. This places the group's PeopleSoft operation roughly four months before its September claim of breaching the FBI.

findings.title: ShinyHunters PeopleSoft Data Theft Campaign Hits 100+ Organizations, Nottingham University Confirms Breach
findings.summary_md: ShinyHunters claimed 300 compromised PeopleSoft instances across more than 100 organizations, telling BleepingComputer it used a gadget chain of old and zero-day vulnerabilities. The University of Nottingham confirmed 454,600 current and former students were affected. Researcher Michael R found exposed staging infrastructure including MeshCentral agents, credential spray scripts, and ransom note tooling.

findings.title: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog (CVE-2026-35273)
findings.summary_md: CISA added the exploited Oracle PeopleSoft vulnerability CVE-2026-35273 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on June 12, 2026, two days after Oracle's patch release. The listing formalized that the flaw was under active attack and set federal remediation deadlines.

findings.title: Oracle Mitigates PeopleSoft Zero-Day Exploited in Data Theft Attacks
findings.summary_md: Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group confirmed ShinyHunters (UNC6240) exploited the PeopleSoft flaw from May 27 through June 9, 2026, notifying over 100 organizations, 68% in US higher education. Entry was via /PSEMHUB/ endpoints, with MeshCentral staging on 142.11.200[.]186-190 masquerading as Azure via azurenetfiles[.]net, zstd-compressed exfiltration over SSH to 176.120.22[.]24, and extortion notes named README-IF-YOU-SEE-THIS-YOUVE-BEEN-HACKED.TXT. Organizations unable to patch were told to disable the Environment Management Hub or block /PSEMHUB/* and /PSIGW/HttpListeningConnector.

findings.title: ShinyHunters claims FBI hack: 'This is NOT financially motivated'
findings.summary_md: First coverage of the FBI claim itself. The group described an Oracle PeopleSoft pre-auth zero-day giving remote code execution on the jobs portal at apply.fbijobs.gov, a claimed 2 TB to 3 TB haul covering current, former, and prospective employees, and lateral movement onto FBI-managed AWS GovCloud servers with access to HR, MedLink, and CJIS services. ShinyHunters demanded the FBI retract its May 2026 FLASH report and defaced the jobs site with a 'This site has been seized by ShinyHunters' message.

findings.title: ShinyHunters claims FBI hack, data theft in PeopleSoft zero-day breach
findings.summary_md: ShinyHunters told BleepingComputer it used the alleged zero-day on a Monday night, then moved laterally into FBI-managed AWS GovCloud infrastructure and compromised FBI Criminal Justice, HR, and Medlink services. It claimed 2 TB to 3 TB of employee, applicant, and internal records, shared a defacement screenshot of apply.fbijobs.gov, and said it was exploiting the same flaw against other organizations including Fortune 500 companies. BleepingComputer could not independently verify the zero-day, lateral movement, or data volume, and the FBI confirmed only that it was investigating unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov.

findings.title: ShinyHunters Renews Mass Exploitation Campaign Targeting Oracle PeopleSoft with WAF Bypass Techniques
findings.summary_md: Google Cloud threat intelligence reported that ShinyHunters renewed mass exploitation of Oracle PeopleSoft using WAF bypass techniques, against a backdrop of more than 100 organizations already targeted via CVE-2026-35273. The report confirmed the campaign persisted months after Oracle's June fix.

findings.title: ShinyHunters uses WAF bypass trick in Oracle PeopleSoft attacks
findings.summary_md: Google's Mandiant and GTIG reported ShinyHunters modified its exploit to bypass WAF rules that block the literal /PSEMHUB/ path by using URL-encoded versions of it, resuming exploitation of unpatched PeopleSoft servers that had relied on WAF mitigation instead of the June security update.
